title: One Seed, Many Streams: Randomness That Does Not Change When You Add a Sensor

questions.question: Why does adding a logging camera to a simulation sometimes change a bug that has nothing to do with it?
options: The camera uses the same seed as the bug, so it reproduces it elsewhere
Logging slows the simulation, and the bug depends on timing
All the parts draw from one generator, so each part's numbers depend on how many draws the others made: with the camera added the imu's noise changed in 1000 of 1000 values
The camera's noise is added to every other sensor's
questions.explanation: With one shared generator, inserting a part that draws numbers shifts everyone else's. The imu's noise did not get worse; it got someone else's.

questions.question: What is the avalanche property of a mixer?
options: Its output can be turned back into its input
The same input always gives the same output
Changing one bit of the input changes about half the output bits: 32.1 of 64 on average here, so neighbouring seeds look unrelated
Its output is always larger than its input
questions.explanation: Seeds 1, 2 and 3 are nearly the same number. A good mixer makes them into three that share nothing, so their streams start differently.

questions.question: How is a part's seed made?
options: From the order in which the parts were created
From the master seed plus the part's index in a list
From the time the part was first used
From the master seed and a hash of the part's name, so it does not depend on which other parts exist or the order they were made in
questions.explanation: A seed that depends only on the master and the name is the same whatever else exists. Adding or reordering parts leaves it alone.

questions.question: What does a seed of zero do to a xorshift generator, and to this stream?
options: Both stay at zero for ever
Both work: zero is as good a seed as any
This stream stays at zero, and a xorshift generator recovers after one draw
A xorshift generator stays at zero; this stream's successive numbers differ, since it adds a constant before mixing
questions.explanation: Xor and shifts of zero are zero, so a xorshift state of zero never leaves it. Adding a constant before mixing moves this one off zero at once.

questions.question: Streams for the encoder and the imu were asked for in opposite orders in two simulations. What happened?
options: The streams swapped: each part got the other's numbers
The motor's and the imu's numbers were identical in both: the order of first asking changes nothing
The second simulation got an error for asking out of order
The first part asked got the same numbers and the second different ones
questions.explanation: A stream is made from the master seed and its own name the first time it is asked for. When that happens makes no difference.

questions.question: What was the correlation between two streams from one master seed?
options: -0.0040: no relationship
1.0000: they are the same stream
0.5000: they share half their bits
-1.0000: one is the mirror of the other
questions.explanation: The encoder's and the imu's numbers from one master seed had no relationship that the correlation could find.
